title: 11.5 A 200MHz-BW Blocker-Tolerant Receiver with Fifth-Order Filtering Achieving 19dBm Adjacent-Channel IIP3
problem: 5G NR receivers with 200+ MHz channel bandwidth must handle strong in-band and adjacent-channel blockers while maintaining low noise figure and acceptable power consumption, requiring aggressive analog filtering before digitization.
motivation: 5G's wide-bandwidth RF channels expose receivers to stringent linearity requirements for blocker rejection, necessitating high-order filtering with minimal power overhead.
method: The receiver uses a five-stage filter (fifth-order filtering) at the input with steep roll-off exceeding 20dB per decade of frequency, which sharply rejects signals from nearby channels before they can interfere. It employs a mixer-first architecture where the incoming radio signal passes through this front-end filter before being converted to baseband (the low-frequency signal containing the data). To keep power consumption low while maintaining the low noise figure needed for weak-signal reception, the design uses stacked capacitors for passive gain—amplifying the signal without drawing extra current.
key_novelty: Five-stage filter architecture that steeply suppresses adjacent-channel interference while using less power than previous mixer-first designs.
contributions: Fifth-order baseband filtering enabling 19dBm adjacent-channel IIP3
Optimized noise figure to power consumption trade-off through passive gain techniques
baselines: Conventional RX architectures with reduced filtering order
primary_theme: High-order filtering receiver for 5G blocker-tolerant wideband reception
